intro: If you're searching for carpal tunnel physiotherapy near you, you're likely dealing with tingling, numbness or pain in your hand and wrist that you want properly assessed and treated. A physiotherapist can guide you through splinting, nerve gliding exercises and activity changes, and will refer you on if your symptoms need further review. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK physiotherapist who quotes you directly, with prices on application.
need_heading: What people searching for carpal tunnel physiotherapy near me usually need
need_lead: Most people want a local physiotherapist who understands carpal tunnel syndrome and can offer practical, hands-on help.
needs: You have numbness or tingling in your thumb, index and middle fingers, especially at night, and want to know whether a night splint could help.
Your symptoms are interfering with work or sleep and you want advice on workstation changes and activity modification.
You have been diagnosed with carpal tunnel syndrome and need physiotherapy to manage symptoms and avoid worsening.
You are recovering from carpal tunnel surgery and need rehabilitation to restore strength and movement.
You want to see a physiotherapist near you who can assess your hand and wrist and discuss whether you need a referral for further medical review.
context_heading: What to understand about carpal tunnel physiotherapy
context: Physiotherapy for carpal tunnel syndrome often involves night splints, nerve gliding exercises and changes to your daily activities, including how you use your workstation. If numbness persists or worsens, your physiotherapist will advise you to seek a medical review.

In the UK, 'physiotherapist' is a protected title, so anyone using it must be registered with the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC). You can check the HCPC register online, and many physiotherapists are also members of the Chartered Society of Physiotherapy (CSP), shown by the letters MCSP.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Describe your main symptoms, such as where you feel numbness or tingling and whether it is worse at night.
Mention how long you have had symptoms and whether they are getting better or worse.
Say whether you have already been diagnosed with carpal tunnel syndrome or are waiting for a diagnosis.
Tell us if you have had any surgery or other treatment for your hand or wrist.
Explain how your symptoms affect your daily life, work and sleep.
Let us know your location so we can introduce you to a physiotherapist near you.
questions: What experience do you have in treating carpal tunnel syndrome?
Will you provide or recommend a night splint, and how should I use it?
What nerve gliding or other exercises should I do, and how often?
What changes can I make at work to help my symptoms?
When would you advise me to see a doctor or seek further medical review?
How will you monitor my progress and adjust the treatment plan?

faqs.q: Can physiotherapy help carpal tunnel syndrome?
faqs.a: Physiotherapy can help manage carpal tunnel symptoms through splinting, nerve gliding exercises and activity changes. If symptoms persist, your physiotherapist may recommend a medical review.

faqs.q: Do I need a referral to see a physiotherapist for carpal tunnel syndrome?
faqs.a: You can often see a physiotherapist without a referral, but some clinics may ask for one. It's best to check when you enquire.

faqs.q: What happens during a physiotherapy appointment for carpal tunnel syndrome?
faqs.a: The physiotherapist will assess your hand and wrist, discuss your symptoms and daily activities, and may provide splinting, exercises and advice. They will also explain what to do if symptoms don't improve.

faqs.q: How do I check if a physiotherapist is qualified?
faqs.a: You can check that your physiotherapist is registered with the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) by searching the online register. Many are also members of the Chartered Society of Physiotherapy (CSP), shown by MCSP after their name.
